symbols.name: P_n
symbols.space: subsets of the law space of \(P\)

symbols.name: hat_g
symbols.role: training-realized treatment fit held fixed in evaluation

symbols.name: hat_q
symbols.role: training-realized outcome fit held fixed in evaluation

symbols.name: Q_P
symbols.role: conditional law of the three evaluation folds for fixed supplied fits

symbols.name: E_Q
symbols.role: evaluation-only expectation conditional on supplied fits

symbols.name: r
symbols.role: residual for the supplied treatment fit

symbols.name: V_env
symbols.role: uniform standard-deviation envelope for calibrated scores

symbols.name: MOM_beta
symbols.def: Writing \(n=m b_n(\beta)+r_\beta\) with \(0\le r_\beta<b_n(\beta)\), \(\operatorname{MOM}_{\beta}(W_1,\ldots,W_n)\) is the \(\lceil b_n(\beta)/2\rceil\)-th order statistic of the averages over consecutive blocks, the first \(r_\beta\) of size \(m+1\) and the remainder of size \(m\)

symbols.name: hat_k4
symbols.def: \(\widehat k_4=\widehat m_4-4\widehat m_1\widehat m_3+12\widehat m_1^2\widehat m_2-6\widehat m_1^4-3\widehat m_2^2\)

symbols.name: C_sel
symbols.role: constant in the finite-sample branch-selection bound

symbols.name: a_A
symbols.role: Appell moment tolerance including lower-moment estimation

novel.justification: This auxiliary nondegeneracy restriction is satisfied by homoskedastic outcome innovations with positive variance and by heteroskedastic models whose conditional scale is uniformly bounded away from zero.
Shrinking fourth-cumulant separation includes smooth Gaussian--Rademacher convolutions and models treatment shocks approaching Gaussianity.

definitions.name: primitive partially linear law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P:P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:outcome-equation},\text{ass:treatment-equation},\text{ass:outcome-orthogonality},\text{ass:independent-treatment-noise},\text{ass:unit-treatment-variance},\text{ass:uniform-envelope}\}\).

definitions.name: conditional supplied-fit radius set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H_n(P)=\{(\widehat g,\widehat q):\|\widehat g-g_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{g,n},\ \|\widehat q-q_0\|_{L^8(P_X)}\le\varepsilon_{q,n}\}\).

definitions.name: conditional projected evaluation experiment
definitions.construction: For each \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and fixed supplied \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\), observe mutually independent \(D_K,D_D,D_A\sim P^n\), with law \(Q_P=P^n\otimes P^n\otimes P^n\).

definitions.name: Gaussian branch
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_n=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:\eta\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\}\).

definitions.name: auxiliary nondegenerate Gaussian subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}=\{P\in\mathcal G_n:P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:outcome-noise-variance}\}\).

definitions.name: fourth-cumulant-separated branch
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal N_n(\delta_n)=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:|\kappa_4|\ge\delta_n\}\).

definitions.name: two-branch union
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal U_n=\mathcal G_n\cup\mathcal N_n(\delta_n)\).

definitions.name: testing and length scales
definitions.construction: \(s_n=n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}^4\), \(d_n=n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\), \(B_n=n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}^3\varepsilon_{q,n}+\varepsilon_{g,n}^4\), \(\Lambda_n=1\) for \(\varepsilon_{g,n}=0\) and \(\Lambda_n=\min\{1,[\{1\vee\log(1/\varepsilon_{g,n})\}/\log(en)]^3\}\) otherwise, and \(d_n^-=n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\).

definitions.name: explicit four-event calibration
definitions.construction: For every \(\beta\in(0,1)\), set \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\). Write \(n=m b_n(\beta)+r_\beta\), where \(0\le r_\beta<b_n(\beta)\), and partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) into consecutive blocks with the first \(r_\beta\) of size \(m+1\) and the remaining blocks of size \(m\); all blocks are nonempty. Let \(\operatorname{MOM}_{\beta}\) be the \(\lceil b_n(\beta)/2\rceil\)-th order statistic of their block averages, set \(V_{\mathrm{env}}=2^{16}(1+C_{\mathrm{env}})^8\), and set \(\rho_n(\beta)=4V_{\mathrm{env}}\sqrt{b_n(\beta)/n}\). Allocate error \(\alpha/4\) to each of \(E_D,E_K,E_A,E_S\); inside \(E_K\), allocate \(\alpha/16\) to each of the four raw residual moments.

definitions.name: split-sample estimated Appell score
definitions.construction: Using the nonempty \(b_n(\alpha/16)\)-block partition in \(\operatorname{MOM}_{\alpha/16}\), for \(j=1,2,3,4\) set \(\widehat m_j=\operatorname{clip}_{[-V_{\mathrm{env}},V_{\mathrm{env}}]}\{\operatorname{MOM}_{\alpha/16}(r_{K,1}^j,\ldots,r_{K,n}^j)\}\); set \(\widehat\mu=\widehat m_1\), \(\widehat v=\widehat m_2-\widehat m_1^2\), \(\widehat c_3=\widehat m_3-3\widehat m_1\widehat m_2+2\widehat m_1^3\), \(\widehat k_4=\widehat m_4-4\widehat m_1\widehat m_3+12\widehat m_1^2\widehat m_2-6\widehat m_1^4-3\widehat m_2^2\), and \(\widehat A_3(u)=(u-\widehat\mu)^3-3\widehat v(u-\widehat\mu)-\widehat c_3\).

definitions.name: calibrated safe DML interval
definitions.construction: Using the nonempty \(b_n(\alpha/4)\)-block partition in \(\operatorname{MOM}_{\alpha/4}\), set \(\widetilde\theta_D=\operatorname{MOM}_{\alpha/4}(\{(Y_{D,i}-\widehat q(X_{D,i}))(T_{D,i}-\widehat g(X_{D,i}))\}_{i=1}^n)\) and \(I_D=[\widetilde\theta_D-a_D,\widetilde\theta_D+a_D]\), where \(a_D=\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}+\rho_n(\alpha/4)\).

definitions.name: calibrated centered Appell inversion
definitions.construction: Using the nonempty \(b_n(\alpha/4)\)-block partition in \(\operatorname{MOM}_{\alpha/4}\), set \(\widehat H_A=\operatorname{MOM}_{\alpha/4}(\{(Y_{A,i}-\widehat q(X_{A,i}))\widehat A_3(r_{A,i})\}_{i=1}^n)\), \(\widehat S_A=\operatorname{MOM}_{\alpha/4}(\{r_{A,i}\widehat A_3(r_{A,i})\}_{i=1}^n)\), \(a_A=8V_{\mathrm{env}}\{\varepsilon_{g,n}^3\varepsilon_{q,n}+\varepsilon_{g,n}^4+\rho_n(\alpha/16)\}+\rho_n(\alpha/4)\), and \(I_A=\{\theta\in[-C_{\mathrm{env}},C_{\mathrm{env}}]:|\widehat H_A-\theta\widehat S_A|\le a_A\}\).

definitions.name: joint high-probability event
definitions.construction: With every median-of-means statistic formed from the nonempty \(b_n(\beta)\)-block partition at its displayed \(\beta\), let \(E_D=\{|\widetilde\theta_D-\theta_0|\le a_D\}\), \(E_K=\bigcap_{j=1}^4\{|\widehat m_j-E_P[r^j]|\le\rho_n(\alpha/16)\}\), \(E_A=\{|\widehat H_A-\theta_0\widehat S_A-E_P[(Y-\widehat q(X)-\theta_0r)\widehat A_3(r)\mid D_K]|\le\rho_n(\alpha/4)\}\), and \(E_S=\{|\widehat S_A-E_P[r\widehat A_3(r)\mid D_K]|\le\rho_n(\alpha/4)\}\), with each conditional expectation holding \(D_K\) and the supplied fits fixed.

definitions.name: split residual-cumulant test
definitions.construction: \(\phi_n=\mathbf1\{|\widehat k_4|>\delta_n/2\}\).

definitions.name: finite-sample branch-selection error envelope
definitions.construction: Fix a universal numerical constant \(C_{\mathrm{sel}}>0\) and set \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}=\min\{1,C_{\mathrm{sel}}[(s_n/\delta_n)^2+\{\rho_n(\alpha/16)/\delta_n\}^2]\}\).

definitions.name: test-and-intersect interval
definitions.construction: \(C_n^*=I_D\) if \(\phi_n=0\); if \(\phi_n=1\), set \(C_n^*=I_D\cap I_A\) when the intersection is nonempty and \(C_n^*=I_D\) otherwise.

definitions.name: branchwise expected-length vector
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal L_n(C_n)=(L_G(C_n),L_N(C_n))\), where \(L_G(C_n)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal G_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}E_{Q_P}|C_n|\) and \(L_N(C_n)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(\delta_n):(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}E_{Q_P}|C_n|\).

definitions.name: attainable honest-length region
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal A_n=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R_+^2:\exists C_n,\inf_{P\in\mathcal U_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}Q_P\{\theta_0\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha,\ L_G(C_n)\le a,\ L_N(C_n)\le b\}\).

definitions.name: Rademacher-partition exponential-Hermite handle
definitions.construction: Use a growing finite partition of \(\mathcal X\), random cell signs, moment-matched nuisance-shift priors, and positive exponential-Hermite tilts of the primitive treatment-residual density; certify support in the primitive branches, the supplied-fit radii, and bounded chi-square distance between the induced projected evaluation mixtures.

definitions.name: multiscale Gaussian-prior handle
definitions.construction: Apply exponential-Hermite nuisance tilts on a geometrically graded Rademacher partition and solve the Gaussian dual weighting program; success requires bounded chi-square distance between projected evaluation mixtures and target displacement of order \(d_n\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and fixed \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\), \(E_P[(Y-\widehat q(X))(T-\widehat g(X))]-\theta_0=E_P[(\widehat g(X)-g_0(X))(\widehat q(X)-q_0(X))]\), whose absolute value is at most \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\).
statements.justification: The identity makes known unit residual variance a safe unnormalized DML branch.
statements.gap: Normalized DML analyses estimate a denominator; this exact identity supplies the coverage-preserving fallback here.
statements.consumer: It gives a valid interval for analysts using slow black-box nuisance fits.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and fixed \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\), \(E_P[A_{3,r}(r)]=0\), \(E_P[rA_{3,r}(r)]=k_{4,r}\), and \(|k_{4,r}-\kappa_4|\le8V_{\mathrm{env}}\varepsilon_{g,n}^4\). Moreover, \(|E_P[(Y-\widehat q(X)-\theta_0r)A_{3,r}(r)]|\le8V_{\mathrm{env}}(\varepsilon_{g,n}^3\varepsilon_{q,n}+\varepsilon_{g,n}^4)\).
statements.justification: These identities derive the denominator and the \(B_n\) remainder for the centered, variance-corrected polynomial.
statements.gap: Fixed-cumulant ACE theory does not give shrinking-denominator control after all lower residual cumulants are estimated independently.
statements.consumer: They permit Appell inversion without treating residual mean, variance, or skewness as known.

statements.statement: If \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), then \(b_n(\alpha/16)=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\) and every calibrated partition has nonempty blocks. Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal U_n\) and fixed \((\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)\), \(Q_P(E_D^c)\le\alpha/4\), \(Q_P(E_K^c)\le\alpha/4\), \(Q_P(E_A^c)\le\alpha/4\), and \(Q_P(E_S^c)\le\alpha/4\); hence \(Q_P(E_D\cap E_K\cap E_A\cap E_S)\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: It makes the simultaneous error allocation for coverage, selection, and length operational.
statements.gap: The closest fixed-cumulant analysis does not calibrate a union-honest pretest and inversion on independent folds.
statements.consumer: It yields auditable finite-sample critical radii depending only on \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), \(n\), and \(\alpha\).

statements.statement: There is a universal numerical choice of \(C_{\mathrm{sel}}>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), \[\max\left\{\sup_{P\in\mathcal G_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}Q_P(\phi_n=1),\ \sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(\delta_n):(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}Q_P(\phi_n=0)\right\}\le p_{\mathrm{sel},n}=\min\left\{1,C_{\mathrm{sel}}\left[(s_n/\delta_n)^2+\{\rho_n(\alpha/16)/\delta_n\}^2\right]\right\}.\]
statements.justification: The explicit two-sided pretest error controls the fallback contribution to non-Gaussian expected length.
statements.gap: Fixed-cumulant ACE bounds do not quantify branch-selection errors for nuisance-contaminated residual cumulants at shrinking separation.
statements.consumer: It lets an interval implementation report a finite-sample upper bound on selecting the wrong score branch.

statements.statement: For every \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), the explicitly calibrated \(C_n^*\) obeys \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal U_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}Q_P\{\theta_0\in C_n^*\}\ge1-\alpha\), \(L_G(C_n^*)\lesssim d_n\), and the finite-sample bound \(L_N(C_n^*)\lesssim\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), where \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\le\min\{1,C_{\mathrm{sel}}[(s_n/\delta_n)^2+\{\rho_n(\alpha/16)/\delta_n\}^2]\}\). Consequently, for fixed \(\alpha\) and \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), if \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\), then \(L_N(C_n^*)\lesssim\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\).
statements.justification: This is the constructive field-tier branchwise upper frontier in a single coherent evaluation experiment.
statements.gap: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis give separate point-estimation results with a cumulant bounded away from zero, and the sibling repository paper gives fixed-separation spectral estimation; neither gives a selected union-honest interval under shrinking separation.
statements.consumer: A DoubleML implementation can retain a safe interval and shorten it only after an independent residual-cumulant diagnostic.

statements.statement: There exists \(c>0\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\), and \(c_{\xi}\), such that every \(C_n\) satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal U_n:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}Q_P\{\theta_0\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) also satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal G_{\xi,n}:(\widehat g,\widehat q)\in\mathcal H_n(P)}E_{Q_P}|C_n|\ge cd_n^-,\] and therefore \(L_G(C_n)\ge cd_n^-\). The conditional variance lower bound defining \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) is used only to keep the outcome channel nondegenerate in this Gaussian expected-length converse; it is not a hypothesis of the upper-frontier theorem.
statements.justification: It records the exact currently supportable Gaussian coordinate with its published logarithmic factor and isolates conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy to the lower experiment.
statements.gap: The JMS Gaussian lower construction informs an honest expected-length bound at \(d_n^-\) on the auxiliary nondegenerate Gaussian subclass, while a full \(d_n\) bound is not established.
statements.consumer: It rules out improvement of the global union-supremum length below the certified Gaussian scale.

statements.statement: Can the Rademacher-partition exponential-Hermite handle construct \(\Pi_{G,n}\) and \(\Pi_{N,n}\), supported on primitive laws in \(\mathcal G_n\) and \(\mathcal N_n(\delta_n)\), together with common fixed supplied fits in the corresponding \(\mathcal H_n(P)\), so that the projected evaluation mixtures have uniformly bounded chi-square distance, hide a fourth-cumulant signal of order \(s_n\), and separate \(\theta_0\) by order \(d_n^-\) for \(\delta_n\lesssim s_n\) and by order \(\min\{d_n^-,B_n/\delta_n\}\) for \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\)?
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing construction for the branch-designated converse.
statements.gap: Existing Hermite-mixture bounds do not enforce the exact PLM law, residual independence, primitive-law support, and common supplied-fit budgets in the same projected experiment.
statements.consumer: A successful pair gives the sharp benchmark for diagnostics-driven causal intervals.

statements.statement: Does the fuzzy-Hermite construction imply that every union-honest interval with \(L_G(C_n)\lesssim d_n\) satisfies \(L_N(C_n)\gtrsim d_n^-\) when \(\delta_n\lesssim s_n\) and \(L_N(C_n)\gtrsim\min\{d_n^-,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\)? Success is uniformity over the projected experiments and supplied-fit set defining \(\mathcal A_n\).
statements.justification: The question exposes the unbuilt converse rather than asserting a promissory lower bound.
statements.gap: Cai and Low do not calculate this learned-residual PLM frontier, while fixed-separation ACE and the sibling spectral paper supply neither a shrinking-separation selector nor an expected-length converse.
statements.consumer: Its resolution supplies the rate benchmark for every cumulant-adaptive interval.

statements.statement: Can the multiscale Gaussian-prior handle prove \(L_G(C_n)\gtrsim d_n\) for every interval honest over \(\mathcal G_n\)? Success requires Gaussian-branch projected mixtures with bounded chi-square distance and \(\theta_0\)-separation \(c\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\) whenever \(\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\gg n^{-1/2}\), without a logarithmic restriction on the radii.
statements.justification: It isolates the precise criterion for upgrading \(d_n^-\) to \(d_n\).
statements.gap: The published Gaussian lower experiment retains \(\Lambda_n\), and no cited result removes it on this class.
statements.consumer: A positive answer closes the only logarithmic gap in the Gaussian coordinate.

statements.justification: It isolates the constructive criterion for strict non-Gaussian shortening.
statements.gap: Fixed-separation ACE does not state a shrinking-signal condition for honest expected-length improvement.
statements.consumer: It gives analysts a conservative threshold for deploying the Appell inversion.

statements.statement: Fix \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\). If \(\varepsilon_{g,n}=\varepsilon_{q,n}=\delta_n=n^{-1/8}\), then eventually \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), \(b_n(\alpha/16)=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), \(\rho_n(\alpha/16)=O(n^{-1/2})\), \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}=O(n^{-3/4})\), \(d_n\asymp d_n^-\asymp n^{-1/4}\), \(s_n\asymp B_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\), and \((L_G(C_n^*),L_N(C_n^*))=(O(n^{-1/4}),O(n^{-3/8}))\). If \(\varepsilon_{g,n}=0\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), then \(\Lambda_n=1\), \(d_n^-=d_n=B_n=n^{-1/2}\), and no rate shortening occurs.
statements.justification: The reductions verify a genuine gain and the perfect-treatment-fit benchmark.
statements.gap: No comparator reports these shrinking-cumulant calculations for one union-honest interval.
statements.consumer: They give calibrated simulation and software checks.

sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed supplied nuisance fits. The observed experiment consists only of three mutually independent evaluation folds with projected law \(Q_P=P^n\otimes P^n\otimes P^n\). Every median-of-means statistic uses \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty near-equal consecutive blocks; the coverage and frontier claims apply for \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\).
sampling_model.units: Each fold contains \(n\) independent superpopulation observations \(Z_i=(X_i,T_i,Y_i)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment obeying \(T=g_0(X)+\eta\), with \(\eta\perp X\) and \(E_P[\eta^2]=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Known unit treatment-residual variance is the nondegeneracy normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The statistical law class contains only primitive laws. The selected training-realized functions are external fixed inputs, and uniformity is over all supplied pairs in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 3.2 and 5.4 give a Gaussian DML lower bound and a fixed-positive-cumulant ACE point-estimation upper bound on separate classes.
Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 characterize expected-length adaptation over unions in Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
The paper obtains composite-hypothesis lower bounds by moment-matched priors and chi-square control of normal mixtures.
Theorem 5 rules out second-order PLM orthogonality under Gaussian residuals, while Theorems 8--10 construct higher-order moments under non-Gaussian residuals.
Theorem 2 establishes coverage and interval-length control for the filtered union, while Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient.

tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\), with conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy confined to its lower subexperiment. The proved contribution is the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier; the sibling repository paper treats fixed-separation spectral estimation, while the fuzzy-Hermite branchwise converse and removal of the Gaussian logarithm remain labelled open-ended questions.

project_justification.gap: Published structure-agnostic PLM theory and the sibling repository paper study separate Gaussian or fixed-non-Gaussian point-estimation classes and fixed-separation spectral constructions, not one conditionally specified projected experiment with union honesty, shrinking cumulant separation, and branchwise expected length.
project_justification.niche: The informative object is the two-coordinate expected-length region; the global union supremum remains governed by the Gaussian coordinate.
project_justification.fill: The proved component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion for the shrinking-separation upper frontier. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is auxiliary to the Gaussian expected-length lower theorem, and the PLM-compatible fuzzy-Hermite converse remains open.

related_work: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis, especially Theorems 3.2 and 5.4 and Appendices D and G, inform the Gaussian lower coordinate and fixed-separation ACE component but do not give a union-honest shrinking-cumulant interval. The auxiliary condition \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) is not attributed to their envelope and is used only for the Gaussian expected-length lower subexperiment. Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik, Theorems 5 and 8--10, inform the Gaussian obstruction and higher-order score. Cai and Low, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, inform branchwise expected length, while their Gaussian model has no learned PLM residual. Cai and Low's 2011 Hermite mixture method informs the fuzzy-prior handle. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman inform localized product-mixture calculations. Chernozhukov et al. supply the split DML benchmark. Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo's Theorem 2 informs filtered-union coverage and interval-length control, while their Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient; neither theorem uses treatment cumulants. The sibling repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\) proves fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions and explicitly leaves shrinking separation, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and a local matching lower bound unresolved. The present proved contribution is instead the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier; it does not claim a matching Pareto frontier. Quessy and Mailhot analyze centered and studentized normality statistics without nuisance-contaminated residuals. Armstrong, Kline, and Sun motivate caution about pretesting for a different point-risk object.
technical_internal_limitation: The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\), not \(d_n\), and uses the auxiliary nondegenerate Gaussian subclass \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\). The upper theorem neither needs the conditional outcome-noise variance lower bound nor identifies a matching Pareto boundary. Its finite-sample guarantee starts at \(n=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), when every requested calibration block count is available. The early kill test is a finite Rademacher-partition exponential-Hermite pair supported on primitive PLM laws, sharing admissible fixed supplied fits, and inducing projected mixtures with bounded chi-square distance and the target displacements in the open-ended question.
honest_scope: The law class is primitive and contains no learner-performance condition. All inference is conditional on fixed supplied fits and uniform over their radius set. The Appell polynomial estimates the first four raw residual moments on a fold independent of inversion. Every median-of-means operator partitions the sample into \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty blocks, and the theorem assumes \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\). Four named events receive error \(\alpha/4\) each, while the separate bound \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\) quantifies wrong-branch selection. The novel auxiliary restriction \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) defines only \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and is used only for the Gaussian expected-length converse, not for the adaptive upper frontier. The sibling repository paper settles fixed-separation spectral estimation, not this local-to-Gaussian union-honest length problem. The branchwise converse and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) are open. No matching Pareto boundary or improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.
seeds: Branchwise honest expected-length upper frontier for Gaussian versus fourth-cumulant-separated treatment noise.
Local-transition limit experiment at the residual-cumulant testing scale.

novelty_justification: The kernel changes the object from separate minimax point errors to two worst-case expected lengths for one interval over a precisely projected evaluation experiment. The primitive law class is separated from fixed supplied-fit radii, and conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is a novel auxiliary restriction confined to the Gaussian expected-length lower subexperiment. Relative to fixed-separation ACE and the repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\), the proved new objects are the shrinking residual-cumulant testing scale, explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, the finite-sample wrong-branch probability envelope, the fully estimated Appell inversion, and the conditional supplied-fit branchwise upper-length vector. The repository paper's fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions do not settle shrinking-separation union honesty. The upper theorem and certified \(d_n^-\) Gaussian coordinate are separated from the open fuzzy-Hermite converse and open removal of \(\Lambda_n\); no matching Pareto frontier is claimed.
